title: Multi-generation defensive-priority SMC: ordering aliasing survives recursion; square-root particle allocation reduces variance at fixed budget

public_sources.title: Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering
public_sources.authors: Randal Douc, Olivier Cappe, Eric Moulines
public_sources.used_for: Published counterexample that systematic resampling lacks uniform variance dominance; stratified/residual improve over multinomial in the analyzed one-step setting.

public_sources.title: Stratification and Optimal Resampling for Sequential Monte Carlo
public_sources.authors: Yichao Li, Wenshuo Wang, Ke Deng, Jun S. Liu
public_sources.used_for: Ordered stratification can reduce resampling variance and is optimal in the stated one-dimensional setting.

public_sources.title: Variance estimation in the particle filter
public_sources.used_for: Particle-filter asymptotic variance decomposes into time-step contributions; varying particle counts permits approximate asymptotically optimal allocation, with genealogy-based variance estimation from a single run.

synthetic_model.initial_representation: 32 particles per state with weights 0.8/32 and 0.2/32, so the initial measure is exact rather than Monte Carlo sampled.
synthetic_model.transition: base P only; no transition-proposal likelihood ratio needed in this experiment

resampling_validation.design: At each generation compute q from the pre-resampling weighted system, reorder particles as score-sorted, alternating low/high priority, or fresh random permutation, resample with iid multinomial, independent stratified uniforms, or one shared-offset systematic uniform, then propagate through base P and G. Correctness follows conditionally from expected offspring counts Mq plus W/(Mq); Monte Carlo means are a numerical check only.

across_generations.interpretation: The shared-offset ordering penalty survives 2-5 recursive generations in this finite-state model. The exact factor is model/order-specific and is not a universal lower bound.

particle_allocation.theorem_level_derivation: If asymptotic variance is approximated by sum_t A_t/N_t and per-particle cost at step t is k_t, minimizing variance subject to sum_t k_t N_t=C yields N_t = C*sqrt(A_t/k_t)/sum_s sqrt(A_s k_s). With equal per-particle costs, N_t is proportional to sqrt(A_t). Predictable N_t chosen before current-generation offspring preserves the conditional unbiasedness argument; outcome-dependent current-generation stopping is not covered.
particle_allocation.pilot: Using independent 6000-repetition finite differences around N_t=64 (one generation changed to 32 or 128 while the others stayed 64) gave engineering A_t estimates [245.2047,81.6926,43.1701,54.8012,44.2172]. These are finite-model pilot estimates, not a single-run theorem-level variance estimator.
particle_allocation.interpretation: At identical total descendant budget, pilot-estimated square-root allocation reduced normalizing-constant variance by about 14.1% in an independent synthetic validation, while reversing the allocation increased variance by about 26.9%. The result supports online generation-wise allocation from genealogy/asymptotic-variance estimates rather than uniform particle counts, but it is not a real-agent benchmark.

negative_scope: Systematic resampling remains unbiased here under the proper expected-count correction; the result concerns variance and ordering sensitivity, not correctness.
The adversarial alternating order is deliberately constructed and does not imply systematic resampling is usually poor.
Stratified ordering is also algorithmic state; its variance is robustly bounded in the one-step theorem but multi-generation total-variance dominance is not claimed.

The square-root schedule used pilot estimates from repeated synthetic runs. Production use should estimate generation-wise variance contributions online, e.g. from genealogy-based estimators, and choose counts predictably from past information.
No claim about AGI capability, real multi-turn agents, human labels, or tool/environment likelihoods follows from this finite-state experiment.
next_action: Replace repeated-run pilot A_t estimates with a role-local single-run/past-only genealogy variance proxy inspired by Lee-Whiteley/ALVar, then choose predictable N_t by the square-root rule and validate under abrupt changes in which the high-variance generation moves over time. Keep independent stratified resampling as the robust default; retain systematic only behind an explicit ordering-randomization/variance test if there is a compelling implementation reason. After this, map the same construction to a finite multi-turn agent trajectory only when base/proposal transition likelihood semantics are explicit.
